questions.prompt: 1. Which time phrase means 4:15?
questions.evidence: Quarter past four means fifteen minutes after four, so 4:15.
questions.objectiveLabel: Telling the time with quarter past and half past

questions.prompt: 2. Which phrase means 6:30?
questions.evidence: Half past six is thirty minutes after six, so 6:30.
questions.objectiveLabel: Telling the time with quarter past and half past

questions.prompt: 3. Which phrase means 8:45?
questions.evidence: Quarter to nine is fifteen minutes before nine, so 8:45.
questions.objectiveLabel: Telling the time with quarter to

questions.prompt: 4. Choose the correct sentence about one quiz show.
questions.evidence: With one programme, such as a quiz show, the verb takes an s: starts.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using start and starts with the right subject
options: The quiz show start at nine.
The quiz show starts at nine.
The quiz show starting at nine.

questions.prompt: 5. Choose the correct sentence about two cartoons.
questions.evidence: A plural subject such as cartoons takes start without an s.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using start and starts with the right subject
options: The cartoons is start at four.

questions.prompt: 6. Choose the correct question.
questions.evidence: After does, the verb stays in its base form: start.
questions.objectiveLabel: Asking “What time does it start?”
options: What time does the film start?
What time does the film starts?

questions.prompt: 7. Which word goes before a clock time such as six o’clock?
questions.evidence: We say at with clock times.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using at with clock times and on with days

questions.prompt: 8. Which word goes before a day name such as Friday?
questions.evidence: We say on with days of the week.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using at with clock times and on with days

questions.prompt: 9. Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.evidence: A sentence starts with a capital letter; football is not a name, so it stays small.
questions.objectiveLabel: Starting sentences with a capital letter and ending with a full stop

questions.prompt: 10. Which programme has questions and prizes?
questions.evidence: A quiz show asks questions and gives prizes.
questions.objectiveLabel: Naming TV programmes

questions.prompt: 11. Which programme shows people making food?
questions.evidence: A cooking programme shows how food is made.
questions.objectiveLabel: Naming TV programmes

questions.prompt: 12. Which sentence says a pupil prefers cartoons?
questions.evidence: With I, the verb prefer has no s.
questions.objectiveLabel: Saying which programme you prefer or like best

questions.prompt: 13. True or false: Quarter to eight means 7:45.
questions.evidence: Quarter to eight is fifteen minutes before eight, which is 7:45.
questions.objectiveLabel: Telling the time with quarter to

questions.prompt: 14. True or false: “The film start at six.” is correct.
questions.evidence: The film is one programme, so the verb needs an s: starts.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using start and starts with the right subject

questions.prompt: 15. True or false: Day names such as Monday begin with a capital letter.
questions.evidence: Day names are proper names, so they start with a capital letter.
questions.objectiveLabel: Starting sentences with a capital letter and ending with a full stop

questions.prompt: 16. True or false: We say “at Friday” to name a day.
questions.evidence: With days, we say on Friday, not at Friday.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using at with clock times and on with days

questions.prompt: 17. Write the time half past eleven in numbers, like 11:30.
questions.evidence: Half past eleven is 11:30.
questions.objectiveLabel: Writing a time in numbers and in words

questions.prompt: 18. Write a sentence that says a programme starts at quarter past nine. Begin with “It starts at”.
questions.evidence: The sentence keeps the time phrase quarter past nine.
questions.objectiveLabel: Writing a complete sentence about a programme time
accepted: It starts at quarter past nine
questions.correct: It starts at quarter past nine
questions.wrongSample: It start at quarter past nine

questions.prompt: 19. Write the missing word: The cooking programme ……… at noon. (start or starts)
questions.evidence: A single programme takes the s ending: starts.
questions.objectiveLabel: Using start and starts with the right subject

questions.prompt: 20. Write a question asking what time a cartoon begins. Use the word does.
questions.evidence: Use “What time does the cartoon start?” with the base form start.
questions.objectiveLabel: Asking “What time does it start?”
accepted: What time does the cartoon start
What time does a cartoon start
questions.correct: What time does the cartoon start
questions.wrongSample: What time does the cartoon starts
